clue.text: Group's honesty oddly absent outside court

indicators.note: one set of letters sits on either side of another, enclosing it
if the odd-numbered letters are missing, only the even-numbered ones remain

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word
CT is a standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A band's integrity goes missing when it appears before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. OET is split so that CT sits between O and ET.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a set of eight, usually eight musicians performing together, so it is a kind of group.

clue.text: Group of players snarled at scorer around end of match

indicators.note: one group of letters goes round another, enclosing it
something snarled is tangled up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A team growls at the player who scored as the game ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of players' suggests a sports team, matching the football-sounding surface, but the players are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large ensemble of musicians playing instruments together, and musicians are players.

clue.text: Often chippy wraps fish

indicators.note: to wrap is to enclose, so the clue words enclose the answer within them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A fish and chip shop usually serves its fish in a paper wrapping.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the join: ofTEN CHippy. A chippy is British slang for a fish and chip shop, which makes 'fish' feel like part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family found in European ponds and rivers.

clue.text: Censure star occasionally that's put on weight

indicators.note: one piece is placed on top of the next, so they join in sequence
occasionally means every so often, so take every other letter

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A celebrity is criticised for having gained weight.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, putting one piece on another places it first.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone can mean to rebuke or scold them severely, a verb sense matching censure.

clue.text: Shocked American turns and runs, followed by terrible spider

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in sequence
to turn round is to face the other way, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: US is short for American

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: An alarmed American spins round and flees from a horrible spider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocked American' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Shocked' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being shocked is being taken aback by something unexpected, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Crew spotted touring before noon

indicators.note: to tour a place is to travel all round it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: spotted means noticed or seen
a.m. means before midday

explanation.surface: A team was seen travelling about in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' looks like it describes the crew, but it is a verb giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors as a body form the working company of a ship, so seamen collectively are its crew.

clue.text: Well-balanced horse race with new leader

indicators.note: a fresh leader replaces the old one, so the opening letter is swapped

parts.note: the Grand National is Britain's most famous steeplechase

explanation.surface: A steady, even-tempered horse runs a race under a different jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is not clued separately; with crossing letters, swapping N for R is the only word that fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-balanced thinks clearly and sensibly, which is what being rational means.

clue.text: Responded about parking and told a fib

parts.note: re means about or concerning
P is the standard sign for parking
telling a fib is lying

explanation.surface: Someone answered a question about a parking offence and told a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like part of the sentence ('responded about'), but it supplies the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to answer, and replied is the matching past tense verb.

clue.text: Prolonged time inside with editor

parts.note: a stretch is slang for a prison sentence
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: An editor serves a long prison term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time inside' is time spent in jail; doing a stretch is serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prolonged has been extended in length or duration, as when a meeting is drawn out.

clue.text: King seized by absolute fear

indicators.note: something seized is gripped and held, so it ends up inside another piece

parts.note: as in dead certain or dead silence, meaning complete
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is gripped by total terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolute' looks like it describes the fear, but it is the outer word: dead means utter or complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great apprehension or terror, a direct noun synonym for fear.

clue.text: Abuse almost constant on X?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
to abuse something is to misuse or maltreat it, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: the word without its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A social media platform called X suffers non-stop abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: X now names a social media site, which suits 'abuse' and 'constant'; here it is just the letter X. The question mark signals definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The letter X is one of the alphabet's non-vowel letters, so it is an example of a consonant.

clue.text: Scrub page with egg on

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: Someone cleans a page that has egg on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on' reads as a breakfast stain, but it is the phrasal verb meaning to encourage.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub can mean to cancel or wipe out entirely, and to purge is to rid or clear away.

clue.text: Deny chances, after losing cases, to improve

indicators.note: a case is an outer covering, so losing it strips off the first and last letters

parts.note: the word without its outer letters
the word without its outer letters

explanation.surface: A barrister refuses opportunities to get better after a run of courtroom defeats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' suggests lawsuits, but here cases are the outer letters of both words.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to raise its quality or value, which is a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Old, short glove daughter left out

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a mitten without its final letter
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A worn, cut-down glove was not passed on to a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left out' sounds like the glove was left outside, but it is the definition. The glove is a mitten, not a mitt.
explanation.definitionFit: Something omitted has been excluded or skipped, so it was left out.

clue.text: The finest shed behind ancient city

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, and behind means at the back, so the last letter goes

parts.note: finest means best

explanation.surface: The best garden hut stands at the back of an old town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a noun for a hut, but it is a verb meaning drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a major city of ancient Greece, and also the name of an ancient Egyptian capital.

clue.text: Cheer North European returning with bottle

indicators.note: to return is to come back the way you went, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north
E is the abbreviation for European
bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian comes home bearing a bottle and is cheered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a drinks container, but in British slang it means nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone on is to give them support and confidence, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Want rigid vessel

parts.note: rigid means stiff or hard
a ship is a sea vessel

explanation.surface: Someone wishes for a sturdy container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' reads as a verb meaning desire; as the definition it is a noun meaning poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of need or poverty describes a state of deprivation and suffering.

clue.text: Favoured match official, under pressure, made a mistake

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece beneath another follows it in the reading order

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure
a ref is a referee
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A popular referee blundered while under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the referee placed under pressure comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something favoured is liked better than the alternatives, which is what preferred means.

clue.text: Cool attitude, for example

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; the definition is used as in 'for instance'

parts.note: in means fashionable or cool
a stance is a position or attitude

explanation.surface: Someone illustrates what a laid-back outlook looks like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' and 'for instance' are interchangeable, so the definition is fair even though it reads as a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case cited to illustrate something, as in the phrase for instance.

clue.text: Mishap this writer had, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: one piece placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: an accent is a way of pronouncing words
this writer is the setter, I, and 'I had' contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: The setter tells of a mishap, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' reads as a stock phrase meaning 'so to speak', but it splits into the container signal and an accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishap is an unlucky event or minor misfortune, and an accident is an unplanned harmful event.

clue.text: Security is raised in warehouse

indicators.note: one piece placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: a depot is a storage building

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters means they read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Security has been tightened at a storage facility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Security is raised' sounds like a heightened alert, but 'Security' is the definition and 'raised' turns over the short word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is money paid as a guarantee, such as a sum held against damage when renting, so it serves as security.

clue.text: Join game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to connect or span a gap
second meaning: a card game played by two pairs

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an invitation to take part in a game; instead the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to span or connect two things; as a noun it names a partnership card game.

clue.text: Comes to grief regularly with long spades

indicators.note: at regular intervals means taking letters at even spacing, every other one

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the word
to long for something is to ache for it
S is the card-game abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A gardener keeps getting into trouble with long-handled spades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes to grief' is an idiom for failing, but it splits: 'Comes to' is the definition and 'grief' is the source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to a place or total is to arrive at it, as in reaching a destination.

clue.text: Dignified Roman leader ignores us

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so letters are dropped

parts.note: Augustus was the first Roman emperor
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A haughty Roman ruler pays no attention to the common people.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letters are the final pair of the emperor's name. The answer is the adjective, not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means respected and impressive, describing someone of venerable bearing.

clue.text: Something that's blown cap inside out, finally

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo it, which is to trump it

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each word concerned

parts.note: the last letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A hat gets blown inside out by the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside out' looks like a reversal or a direction to take outer letters, but it is just two words whose final letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet is a brass instrument played by blowing air through it with buzzing lips.

clue.text: Refill pot, potentially?

parts.note: surface reading: filling a pot again, perhaps with tea
setter's reading: in a down entry, a three-letter word written bottom to top would read as the clue's container word

explanation.surface: Someone needs to fill up the teapot again.
explanation.walkthrough: Read TOP upwards in this down slot and it spells POT, so the answer is an instruction that would produce a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To top up a glass or tank is to fill it again to the brim, so it means refill.

clue.text: A Parisian welcomes a fight in the dark

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: une is French for a
taken as written
a war is a large fight

explanation.surface: A Parisian woman invites a brawl at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the dark' sounds like a place for the fight, but it is the definition, meaning ignorant.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is an idiom for being ignorant of something, which is being unaware.

clue.text: Put up with a US president wanting Greenland, essentially

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing

parts.note: Joe Biden was the 46th US president

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so take the central letter

parts.note: the fifth of the word's nine letters

explanation.surface: Tolerating an American leader who covets Greenland, at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to a different president known for wanting Greenland, but the letters need Biden.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to tolerate or endure it, the same sense as putting up with it.

clue.text: Designs aircraft base rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: planes are aircraft
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Blueprints for an airfield were turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like an airbase in this aviation surface, but it is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: Designs in the sense of drawings or schemes for something to be built are plans.

clue.text: Muddy huge train getting more filthy

indicators.note: to muddy something is to stir it up and cloud it, so the letters get mixed

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A giant steam train becomes grimier as it runs through the mud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filthy' suggests dirt, matching the muddy train, but here it means rude or smutty.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy can mean obscene or risqué, and naughtier is a comparative meaning more indecent.

clue.text: Most attractive quiet street — it's round the bend

parts.note: p is the musical marking for piano, meaning quiet

indicators.note: round the bend is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: The loveliest silent road has a bend in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street' wants to be ST, but the whole word goes into the jumble; the 's of it's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being the most attractive means being the best-looking, the superlative of pretty.

clue.text: Golfer unhappy about unfinished trap

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so the last letter goes
about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: unhappy means sad
a net is a trap, here without its last letter

explanation.surface: A golfer is upset about a bunker he couldn't quite get out of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' suggests a golf bunker, fitting the surface, but here it is a net.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam Snead was a leading American professional golfer who won a record number of PGA Tour events.
